cells.tense: Something here has finished, and you are standing in the open it left.
cells.act: open the door to the next thing on time, not early
cells.ask: There is a next thing here. Take its first step at the size it actually is — just the piece that belongs to today, not the version you'd map out weeks ahead.
cells.core:
A cycle closing cleanly looks like this: the last piece is finished, nothing gets carried past it, and what comes next arrives without being pulled. What came down here took its form from a premise that stopped holding, which is why it went quickly. There is no wreckage underneath — there is open ground, and what fills it has some say in the filling.

The work now is timing. Close what has already closed, and let the next arrival come at its own pace rather than dragging it forward because the gap feels like a reproach. You don't need the whole chapter. When the door is here, you walk through. A cycle ending isn't a verdict on you. It's the form a thing takes when it's done.
cells.sheetLine: The cycle closed. The ground is yours.
cells.verb: finishing a cycle so the next one can begin
cells.place: where what couldn't hold has come down

cells.tense: You are bracing for an ending that hasn't finished arriving yet.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: An ending you've already announced as done — meet it as still happening. Let today's part of it be this size, and skip the closing lines.
cells.core:
A cycle ending at its own speed looks like this: you are in the last of it, not past it, and what follows waits without your pulling. Here, you can see the finish and you've started living beyond it — talking like it's over, planning from the far side, moving as though the last stretch doesn't need you. The clearing is real. It isn't finished.

What's coming is still coming. Meet the day you're actually in, not the one you've already moved on to, and give the ending its hour. Whatever waits beyond this will hold. The risk isn't missing the next chapter. It's not being at this one when the last part closes.

cells.tense: A door closed behind you and you are still standing at its frame.
cells.act: notice what is newly here, right now
cells.ask: Once today, find one thing near you that wasn't near you a season ago. Note it to yourself in a single sentence, then leave it be.
cells.core:
A cycle ending cleanly looks like this: you stand in what the break let in, and the next thing gets its footing because the space is in use. Here, what couldn't hold has come down, and the open space is real — but you keep watching the old frame for the part that hasn't arrived, because letting it end feels like losing it. So the cycle stays half-open and nothing new takes hold.

Nothing needs pushing. What's arriving is arriving. Look once today at what's already around you — the table, the light, the people or the quiet — and find one thing that wasn't around a season back. That's the frame coming down. The next thing doesn't need your permission. It needs the space used.

cells.tense: You're writing in a room you think is still blank, and some of it isn't.
cells.act: let go of the thing you are gripping
cells.ask: Set down what you're still carrying that's over. A drawer, a page, a box — someplace it can rest while you get on.
cells.core:
A cycle ending cleanly looks the same on both sides: it ends, you set it down, your hands are free for whatever comes, and nothing dramatic gets made of it. Here, some cycles have closed and some haven't, and you narrate both the same way. The telling is what keeps either version standing.

You don't have to sort out which is which. Choose a thing you're holding that is over, and put it down — not as loss, as a hand unclenching. The grip was doing more work than the thing was. Then watch what your hands do, and give them space a little. Empty is how the next thing gets picked up.
